newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slip, grades remain weak to close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slip, grades remain weak to close.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes ended weaker Tuesday in both outright prices and grade differentials.
Traders said the slide in domestic grades was notable for Midland/WTI and in the sour markets.

"The continuing weakness in the Midland is beyond bizarre, it's not like it's the last day before scheduling," said one broker, who confirmed the Midland sold at a 40 cents discount to the benchmark, steady to slightly off the Monday levels.
Outright March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing declined around 20 cts to close out at $23.95-$24.05, steady from the late morning when weaker prices were established.
Grade prices ended with the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 16-20 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing, with the final deals at 15 cts over the marker, 5-10 cts lower than Monday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was discussed at a 40-50 cts discount, steady from latest deals.
West Texas Sour/Midland retreated a few cents from Monday to end at a $2.30-34 discount, with the Eugene Island sold late at a $2.50 discount to the marker, 30-40 cts off.
March Postings Plus sold between $2.26-28, 1-3 cts higher than the Monday close, and talked late at $2.29-32.
Continued weakness was seen in the sours from abundant supplies, and rumors West Coast heavy crudes may be offered into the Gulf Coast.
Data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed crude stocks building more than 6 million barrels for the week ended January 31.
Distillate stocks fell more than 4 million barrels, twice the drop that traders expected before the report's release.
